O=C(CCc1ccccc1)Nc1cc(F)ccc1C(=O)C(F)(F)F
It's an amide formed from:
Amine part: c1cc(F)ccc1C(=O)C(F)(F)F -> 4-(trifluoroacetyl)-3-fluoroaniline? Wait, C(=O)C(F)(F)F is a trifluoroacetyl group attached to the phenyl ring. So the amine is H2N-c1cc(F)ccc1C(=O)C(F)(F)F.
Acid part: O=C(CCc1ccccc1) -> 3-phenylpropanoic acid (hydrocinnamic acid).

Wait, the context says "Oxidations". How does this relate to oxidation?
Maybe the amine was oxidized from something? Or the acid was oxidized?

Input: Cc1cc(C=O)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1

Wait, all these examples show Product -> Reactant where Reactant has a less oxidized group than Product? No, wait.
In retrosynthesis, Input is the PRODUCT. Answer is the REACTANTS.
So if Input is O=C(CCc1ccccc1)Nc1cc(F)ccc1C(=O)C(F)(F)F, and the reaction type is Oxidations, then the reactants should be LESS oxidized than the product.
